LeafByte.A small tool for a lighter web.BUILT FOR GREEN SHIFT HACKS · 2026

THE DETAILS MATTER

Small files.
Clear claims.

LeafByte creates real image encodings in your browser and compares their decoded pixels. It keeps the original if no smaller candidate meets your selected similarity floor.

How similarity works

Original and output are compared at the selected output dimensions, then compared in nine full-resolution patches, up to 128 × 128 pixels each, across a 3 × 3 grid. SSIM is calculated on luminance in local 8 × 8 blocks. Small images have overlapping patches. A score near 1 indicates similar sampled structure. This metric can miss fine text, color changes and artifacts, and it does not assess detail lost during resizing. Always inspect your output.

How the budget works

The smallest acceptable candidate for each image forms the minimum bundle. With a budget, LeafByte greedily upgrades image similarity within that limit. This is a heuristic, not a globally optimal quality allocation. When the minimum exceeds your budget, the app retains the similarity floor and reports the shortfall.

What the numbers mean

Byte counts and hashes describe actual input and output files. Transfer scenarios multiply their difference by an editable number of complete, uncached bundle transfers. File reduction is not a measured electricity or carbon reduction. Optimization itself also uses computing resources.

Formats and privacy

Static JPEG, PNG and WebP are supported. Animated images are rejected. Canvas encoding can remove metadata and change color profiles. JPEG output composites transparency on white. Encoders and output sizes vary between browsers. Local files are processed in memory; the app has no analytics or image-upload endpoint. Hosting receives normal page requests.

Demo images

The sample pack contains credited public images. Its results are a software benchmark, not measured real-world environmental savings.
